articles.title: Desvelan el mensaje de la madre de Messi a Nico Paz: "Tú eres el sucesor de mi hijo"
articles.standfirst: Fabián Paz, tío de Nico Paz, cuenta el inédito diálogo entre el futbolista del Como y Celia Cuccittini,
articles.summary: Fabián Paz, tío de Nico Paz, cuenta el inédito diálogo entre el futbolista del Como y Celia Cuccittini,
articles.body: El canario Nico Paz, jugador del Como 1907 al que el Real Madrid podría recuperar con una cláusula unilateral de 80 millones de euros, se postula a base de goles para ser el sucesor de Leo Messi con el mítico número 10 de la selección de Argentina. Fabián Paz, tío de Nico Paz, desveló un inédito diálogo entre el futbolista del Como y Celia Cuccittini, la madre de Leo Messi, tras el triunfo por 3-0 ante Benin el 6 de octubre: "Cuando lo fui a ver a la despedida de Messi, Nico salió del vestuario y estaba la mamá de Messi emocionada, llorando. Nico la va a saludar porque la conocía y ella le agarró la mano y le dijo: 'Vos sos el sucesor de mi hijo'. El tío de Nico aseguró en 'Radio La Red' que el canterano del Real Madrid salió "shockeado" tras las palabras de la madre de Messi en un momento que el propio Nico Paz describió como "muy increíble". Fabián Paz, conocido diseñador y fundador de la marca 'Atelier Pucheta', compartió que "Nico es una persona muy tranquila y sencilla. Él no tiene en la cabeza ser el sucesor de Messi. Para él lo máximo fue conocerlo y jugar con Leo y eso fue como tocar el cielo con las manos". El diseñador destacó sobre Nico Paz que "al no vivir en Argentina no tiene tanta presión como otros jugadores. Aquí el fútbol se vive con una pasión y locura únicas y él se sorprende mucho de eso todavía". Nico Paz es el principal candidato a heredar la mítica camiseta con el número 10 de la albiceleste que con anterioridad lucieron genios con Leo Messi, Diego Armando Maradona, Mario Kempes o Juan Román Riquelme. "La verdad que no pienso en ello (en heredar la camiseta con el 10), lo que pienso es en disfrutar días como hoy... Divertirme en el campo que lo que más amo es jugar al fútbol y encima representando a la selección y representando a tanta gente... juego para eso y quiero seguir haciéndolo", respondió el ex del Madrid, que jugó con el número 18 y lleva cuatro goles en solo 48 días al marcar ante Bolivia, Burkina Faso, Benín y Costa Rica.

articles.title: El derbi pone nota al mercado
articles.standfirst: Cuatro fichajes de Sevilla y Betis son fijos, mientras que nadie termina de asentarse en la delantera
articles.summary: Cuatro fichajes de Sevilla y Betis son fijos, mientras que nadie termina de asentarse en la delantera
articles.body: El derbi hispalense de este sábado supondrá un examen de nivel para los proyectos de Sevilla y Betis. Asimismo, pondrá a prueba la adaptación de una extensa nómina de incorporaciones por parte de ambos clubes. En total, hasta 14 de esos 15 fichajes vivirán su bautismo de fuego en uno de los partidos más intensos del fútbol europeo. Sin embargo, algunos no solo se han asentado en sus equipos, sino que tienen experiencia en varios de los clásicos más pasionales del planeta. En el banquillo local, Luis García Plaza dirigirá su primer derbi sevillano, a diferencia de un Pellegrini que ya acumula trece. A pesar de que es novato en esta rivalidad, se ha enfrentado al Betis en 14 ocasiones durante su trayectoria. Eso sí, su bagaje profesional en los duelos vecinales se limita a su etapa en el Levante, con dos derbis ante el Valencia saldados con un empate y una derrota. El técnico madrileño ya le ha otorgado a esta cita la etiqueta de "el derbi de los derbis". El Sevilla sostiene una buena parte de su estructura competitiva sobre tres refuerzos que se han vuelto indiscutibles. Juan Iglesias ha jugado todas las jornadas de Liga, convirtiéndose en el cuarto futbolista con más minutos y en uno de los líderes del vestuario. Por la otra banda, Félix Correia se ha adueñado del extremo izquierdo gracias a su disciplina táctica, su compromiso colectivo y su habilidad para el balón parado. El rendimiento del luso ha ido de menos a más y ya ha conseguido dos goles y dos asistencias. En el centro del campo, Youssouf Fofana ha elevado el techo competitivo de los sevillistas. En nueve partidos acumula un gol y tres asistencias. Atraviesa su peor momento de forma desde que aterrizó, por lo que el parón de selecciones tiene que haberle servido para tomar oxígeno y recuperar las buenas sensaciones. Además, en Milán disputó seis veces el Derby della Madonnina ante el Inter, siendo titular en todas ellas con seis victorias y un empate. En el Betis, el fichaje más destacado de la temporada y el único fijo en el once es Fran García. El lateral solo se ha perdido dos encuentros entre todas las competiciones (Getafe y Celta) y le ha dado empaque a una posición en la que nadie ofrecía tantas prestaciones desde la salida de Álex Moreno hace ya casi cuatro años. Durante sus tres campañas con el primer equipo del Real Madrid participó en siete derbis ante el Atlético de Madrid. Tanto Sevilla como Betis han tenido más dudas en la delantera. Lucas Stassin parte con ventaja para jugar desde el inicio en el conjunto nervionense. El belga debutó con gol en Cornellá antes de que una lesión frenara su progresión. Su visión y su capacidad asociativa se reflejan en sus dos asistencias con la selección sub-21. Sabe lo que es anotar un doblete en el derbi del Ródano entre Saint-Étienne y Olympique de Lyon. La otra alternativa de Luis García Plaza para la delantera es Robbie Ure. A su refuerzo más caro (6,5 millones de euros) le está costando arrancar. Lleva dos goles y dos asistencias, pero también es el único que ha disputado todas las citas entre Liga y Copa, así como el octavo de la plantilla con más minutos. Inédito con Escocia en la última ventana internacional, lo normal es que salte al césped en la segunda parte del derbi. Si el fichaje más costoso en el Sevilla fue Ure, en el Betis lo fue Troy Parrott (16 millones de euros). Aunque arrancó muy bien, se ha ido apagando y no ha aprovechado la lesión del Cucho. En 13 partidos suma dos goles y una asistencia, anotando el último el 8 de septiembre ante el Lille. Con Irlanda refuerza su confianza, ya que viene de meterle dos tantos a Kosovo. En cuanto a derbis, con el Excelsior le marcó al Feyenoord y al Sparta de Róterdam, mientras que con el MK Dons lo hizo ante el Wimbledon en uno de los derbis más tensos de Inglaterra. Uno de los que suele aspirar al once inicial del Sevilla es Giorgi Kochorashvili, por quien el club invirtió 4,5 millones de euros. El georgiano casi siempre le da al equipo lo que necesita, viéndose relegado al banquillo cuando su entrenador alinea a los dos delanteros. Por su parte, Jon Guridi encadena tres jornadas sin aparecer tras ser titular en cinco de las seis primeras con un nivel más que aceptable. El exfutbolista de la Real Sociedad ha jugado dos derbis vascos en la élite contra el Athletic. Por parte del Betis, Facundo Bernal llegó como relevo de Sergi Altimira por 9,5 millones de euros. Fue titular en siete de los primeros once partidos del Betis hasta que su enganchón con Lamine Yamal le costó una sanción de cuatro encuentros. Curtido en rivalidades como el Fla-Flu o el clásico entre Defensor Sporting y Danubio, es una apuesta importante del club que ha dejado entrever su potencial y debe seguir creciendo en su primer año en Europa. El único fichaje que ya conoce el derbi sevillano es Dani Ceballos. En su anterior etapa disputó seis, pero no pudo salir victorioso, por lo que ganas no le faltan. El utrerano, que cumplió su sueño de regresar a casa, ha dejado muestras de su calidad y cada vez participa más minutos seguidos. No obstante, tiene molestias musculares y es duda para el sábado. Por último, hay otros fichajes con escasas opciones de jugar el Gran Derbi. Uno de ellos es Sanganté, que ha dejado más sombras que luces al combinar despistes defensivos con su poderío físico. Bastante mejor sin balón, tras la grave lesión de Carmona es el único capaz de darle descanso a Juan Iglesias. Su experiencia en los duelos de máxima rivalidad se concentra en cinco derbis normandos entre Le Havre y Caen. Los que menos han participado en ambos equipos son Fran González, Julio Díaz y Diego Conde. Con los jóvenes sevillistas se tendrá paciencia, pues son inversiones de futuro, mientras que el guardameta bético se estrenó en Copa del Rey -al igual que Fran- y se antoja difícil que tenga oportunidades ante el momento de forma de Álvaro Valles. Fichajes consagrados y apuestas de futuro en ambos proyectos. El Sánchez-Pizjuán dictará si los nuevos protagonistas están a la altura del escenario.

articles.title: Una revuelta popular acaba con la polémica X del Leicester, que se ve obligado a recular
articles.standfirst: La polémica saltó después de que el patrocinador club nombrara una "estrella porno internacional (Eva Elfie)" como embajadora
articles.summary: La polémica saltó después de que el patrocinador club nombrara una "estrella porno internacional (Eva Elfie)" como embajadora
articles.body: El Leicester City ha decidido poner fin a su acuerdo con el polémico patrocinador BC.GAME seis meses antes de lo previsto. A principios de este mes, los aficionados expresaron su indignación y consternación después de que el patrocinador de apuestas que aparece en la camiseta del club nombrara a una "estrella porno internacional (la creadora rusa de contenido para adultos Eva Elfie)" como su nueva embajadora. 'The Foxes Trust', un conocido grupo de animación del Leicester City, expresó su "consternación" ante la noticia confirmada por BC.GAME de nombrar a Eva Elfie como su embajadora. El Leicester ha optado por concluir la colaboración, una medida que ha sido bien recibida por los seguidores. "La decisión es el resultado de conversaciones constructivas entre ambas partes durante los últimos días, en las que constatamos que nuestras prioridades comerciales de cara al futuro son diferentes. Queremos agradecer a BC.GAME su apoyo a lo largo de sus dos años y medio de colaboración con el Leicester City, así como el enfoque constructivo que han adoptado para llegar a este acuerdo. Los aficionados que hayan adquirido una réplica de la camiseta con la marca BC.GAME a través de los canales de venta oficiales del LCFC en los últimos 28 días (desde el 21 de octubre de 2026) pueden devolverla para obtener un reembolso completo o realizar un cambio (sujeto a disponibilidad) hasta el miércoles 2 de diciembre", informó el Leicester en un comunicado. La empresa de casinos 'on line' había sido el patrocinador principal de la camiseta de los 'Foxes' desde el inicio de la temporada 2024-25.

articles.title: Figo: "Vinicius volverá a su nivel y a su estatus por la calidad que tiene"
articles.standfirst: El portugués elogia el trabajo defensivo de Diomande, destaca la regularidad de Güler y atribuye a Mourinho parte del mérito por la solidez del Madrid
articles.summary: El portugués elogia el trabajo defensivo de Diomande, destaca la regularidad de Güler y atribuye a Mourinho parte del mérito por la solidez del Madrid
articles.body: Luis Figo está convencido de que Vinicius volverá a ser decisivo en el Real Madrid. El brasileño ha empezado la temporada lejos de su mejor versión y cumple una sanción de cuatro partidos en Liga. El Balón de Oro de 2000, que vistió las camisetas del Barcelona y del Madrid, confía en que recuperará su sitio. "Vinicius es un jugador que volverá a su nivel, a su estatus, por la calidad que tiene", afirmó en declaraciones a Betfair, firma de la que es embajador. Figo encuadra el bajón en las rachas que atraviesa cualquier futbolista y tiene claro cómo acabará esta: "Seguro que volverá a su puesto, a su rendimiento normal. Y volverá a ser un jugador desequilibrante". En marzo ya salió en su defensa, cuando el brasileño falló un penalti ante el Manchester City en la ida de los octavos de final de la Champions. "¿Un consejo para Vinicius y los penaltis? Seguir tirándolos. Sólo fallan los penaltis quienes los tiran", dijo entonces. En la vuelta, Vinicius tuvo otro penalti, volvió a pedir la pelota y marcó. Luego hizo el segundo gol del Madrid, que ganó 1-2. La sanción del brasileño ha abierto un hueco para Yan Diomande. Figo ve al costamarfileño cada vez más asentado en un club exigente y cree que ha sacado partido de la continuidad. "Ahora está jugando más asiduamente y, sin duda, es un jugador desequilibrante, rápido, que tiene gol". El portugués destaca que busca la profundidad y que también responde cuando toca defender: "Tiene una cosa importante para todos los aficionados del Madrid: que se implica en la parte defensiva". Figo encuentra otro ejemplo en Arda Güler. Con más minutos, el turco ha ganado peso en el equipo y ha podido mostrar con regularidad lo que aporta con balón. "Es un jugador que es importante en la fase de construcción del equipo por su calidad técnica, por ser un jugador al que le gusta construir el juego", explicó el exfutbolista. La mejora defensiva con Mourinho Figo atribuye parte del buen momento del Madrid a las decisiones de José Mourinho. A su juicio, los cambios de jugadores y los ajustes en la presión han dado más solidez al equipo y se han traducido en resultados. El portugués reparte el mérito entre el entrenador y la plantilla y sitúa al Madrid entre los equipos más en forma de Europa. La diferencia, según Figo, está en lo que hace el equipo cuando pierde la pelota. "Lo que ha cambiado, yo creo, es la implicación de todos los jugadores en la parte defensiva", apuntó. Con la calidad que tiene arriba, al Madrid le resulta fácil generar ocasiones y marcar. Ahora, añade el portugués, concede menos oportunidades al rival, una de las razones por las que ha prolongado su buena racha.

articles.title: Cassano carga contra el regreso de Ronaldinho al fútbol profesional: “Fue una farsa ridícula”
articles.standfirst: El brasileño, de 46 años y accionista minoritario del Ravenna, disputó 45 minutos en la victoria ante el Forlì en la tercera división italiana
articles.summary: El brasileño, de 46 años y accionista minoritario del Ravenna, disputó 45 minutos en la victoria ante el Forlì en la tercera división italiana
articles.body: Ronaldinho volvió a jugar un partido oficial a los 46 años y Antonio Cassano fue de los más duros con su reaparición. El brasileño disputó 45 minutos con el Ravenna en la victoria ante el Forlì, en la tercera división italiana, después de once años sin competir en un encuentro oficial. El regreso se celebró en el Calcio y el exmadridista lo calificó de “una farsa ridícula”. Cassano empezó por situar al brasileño entre los mejores futbolistas de todos los tiempos. “Quiero empezar diciendo una cosa, y es que tengo un gran respeto por Ronaldinho, como persona y como jugador. Para mí, sigue estando entre los cinco más grandes de la historia, junto a Messi, Maradona, Ronaldo y, probablemente, Pelé”, dijo el italiano en Viva El Futbol, el programa que comparte con Daniele Adani y Nicola Ventola. El episodio se tituló Nazionale tra dubbi e certezze, Pio Esposito e il ritorno di Ronaldinho. La relación con el presidente del Ravenna Ronaldinho es accionista minoritario del Ravenna y amigo personal de su presidente, Ignazio Cipriani. Cassano apuntó a esa relación y especuló con que también hubiera un motivo económico. “Pero lo que hizo el otro día fue muy, muy desagradable de ver. A los 46 años, en esas condiciones, ¿qué se supone que iba a hacer? No lo entendí. Lo hizo porque tiene una relación con Cipriani, que es amigo suyo. Y porque le dieron mucho dinero. No lo sé. Para mí, fue una farsa ridícula. No sé qué otra interpretación darle”, declaró. El exdelantero de Milan, Roma y Real Madrid se puso en el lugar del brasileño. “No lo habría hecho ni aunque me hubieran ofrecido 10 millones. Ni siquiera 20. Me sorprendió ya que siempre fue humilde y uno de los más grandes de la historia. Si me piden que juzgue específicamente lo que pasó, para mí fue una vergüenza, una buffonata”, sentenció.

articles.title: Wales v Norway: Ceri Holland in squad for Women's World Cup play-off final
articles.summary: Ceri Holland is in the Wales squad for next month's Women's World Cup play-off final against Norway despite being out since September through injury.
articles.body:
Ceri Holland has been named in the Wales squad for next month's Women's World Cup play-off final against Norway despite being out since September through injury.

Olivia Clark, Hayley Ladd, Rhiannon Roberts and Ella Powell are also included after fitness issues, but Ffion Morgan, Laura Hughes and Scarlett Hill are among those who miss out with injuries.

The versatile Holland, arguably Wales' most influential player, has been out with a muscle problem, though she is thought to be close to returning to action for club side Liverpool.

Her involvement is a major boost for Wales as they attempt to reach the Women's World Cup for the first time.

Rhian Wilkinson's side face Norway at the Cardiff City Stadium on Tuesday, 1 December, before the return leg in Oslo four days later.

Women's World Cup qualifying play-off final first leg

Live on BBC iPlayer, BBC One Wales, BBC Sounds, BBC Radio Wales, Radio Cymru, BBC Sport website and app, plus live text commentary.

Leicester goalkeeper Clark and Sunderland defender Roberts are also included even though they have not played since September, but the loss of promising Manchester United defender Hill is a blow given her impressive displays against Albania.

Crystal Palace's Ladd and Powell, of Bristol City, have played for their clubs since missing Wales' World Cup play-off semi-final games against the Albanians last month.

Winger Morgan had returned to action for West Ham after not being involved against Albania, but she is back on the sidelines after getting injured while playing for the Hammers last weekend.

Like Southampton midfielder Hughes, Mia Ross – who is without a club after leaving Charlton in September - is missing again, while Fulham full-back Charlie Estcourt is another absentee.

There is also no place for Sunderland defender Tara Bourne, who has switched allegiance from England to Wales but is injured.

There is a recall for once-capped teenager Gwen Zimmerman, who plays for American side Northwestern NCAA, while Newcastle youngster Casi Gregson is included again after winning her first cap against Albania.

Wales start Nations League with home double-header

Wales in fight to retain rising female stars

Wolves midfielder Chloe Williams keeps her place having been a late call-up for the semi-final, while the only uncapped player in the squad is third-choice goalkeeper Soffia Kelly.

Wales are hoping to cause an upset as they bid to reach the Women's World Cup for the first time, though beating former champions Norway may not be enough to guarantee a place in Brazil next summer.

The complex nature of the qualification process means that Wales may have to negotiate inter-confederation play-offs next February to secure a World Cup place, even if they triumph over Norway.

articles.title: Greg Sankey ruled college football. Now, he’s losing grip on SEC | Opinion
articles.summary: Greg Sankey is grumbling about TV broadcasters while the SEC comes unglued. What happened to the SEC's powerful commissioner?
articles.body:
Greg Sankey has been hailed as the smartest person in the room, a man who could see around corners, but the longer his interview on "The Paul Finebaum Show" went, the more disconnected and aloof the SEC 's veteran commissioner sounded.

It's the final question that gets you, isn't it?

Sankey joined "Finebaum" last week to discuss the College Football Playoff expanding to 24 teams, but he finished with a petty diatribe about television announcers .

Sankey came off like your cantankerous neighbor who grumbles that the color commentator stinks.

"I am highly disappointed in announcers and their criticisms (of officiating)," Sankey seethed. "Some of the worst officials in America are those in the announcers' booth."

It is here I realized Sankey lost the plot, and he wears a hollow crown.

How many SEC athletics directors, chancellors and university presidents are thinking that, too?

In COVID times, SEC membership stood united behind Sankey's leadership. He no longer commands the same respect.

In the latest affront to the commissioner's power, LSU basketball rostered ex-pro RJ Luis and played him in defiance of Sankey and the SEC.

Sankey used to be labeled college football's most powerful person. Now, he's just your next-door Average Greg, shaking his fist at the sky, debating whether refs screwed the pooch, and complaining about the broadcasters.

The commissioner who saved a college football season amid a global pandemic has, slowly but surely, lost his grip on his conference and become the target of criticism and insubordination within SEC ranks.

Sankey failed to achieve on two main objectives the past few years. He's come up empty-handed in his yearslong quest to achieve federal legislation to govern NIL, transfer free agency and eligibility.

He also couldn't secure a 16-team College Football Playoff, and so the SEC ultimately acquiesced to a 24-team playoff plan that the Big Ten spawned.

Fifteen months ago, USA TODAY anointed Sankey as the most powerful figure inside college football .

"My responsibility is to be influential and effective," Sankey told me during a 2025 interview .

The past year and a half, Sankey's been neither as influential as he used to be, nor particularly effective on big-ticket items.

He's not even the most effectual or influential commissioner. That would be Big Ten boss Tony Petitti . Sankey's fingerprints were all over the 12-team playoff. The 24-team bracket will be remembered as Petitti's brainchild.

Unrest forms within the SEC, while Greg Sankey's power wanes

Sankey's failures came at a cost, and I don't just mean all the money wasted traveling to Washington D.C., glad-handing with politicos, or golfing with President Trump .

As Sankey became distracted by the politics rat-race, with little to show for his efforts, his clout eroded at home, and fissures formed with the SEC.

LSU and the SEC remain in a state of open imbroglio, playing tit-for-tat in courts of law. LSU playing Luis amounts to a middle finger to Sankey's authority.

If that's not enough to make you question Sankey's grip, Oklahoma athletic director Roger Denny fired a shot across the commissioner's bow last weekend. In a middle-of-the-night tweet, Denny rebuked Sankey for the conference's decision to postpone the Mississippi-Oklahoma game to Sunday, after an FAA ground stop Friday delayed Ole Miss' travel schedule.

Denny fumed that Sankey gave Oklahoma an ultimatum to either forfeit or move the game Sunday to accommodate Ole Miss.

The SEC levied no fines or penalties to Oklahoma or Denny for his comments, a conference spokesperson confirmed.

Longtime SEC observers would struggle to think of a comparable instance of a sitting athletic director so publicly blasting the conference's commissioner.

Oklahoma's iconic ex-coach Bob Stoops described Sankey's decision as "absolutely wrong."

For so long, conflicts and disagreements within the SEC's ranks were kept behind closed doors. Now, dirty laundry is aired on the front lawn for the entire industry to see. Grievances spill into social media blasts or become lawsuit fuel.

The Big Ten looks cohesive, by comparison.

Petitti unified his membership behind a 24-team playoff, and then, one by one, secured favor from the other Power Four conferences until it became reality, despite widespread opposition from fans.

In this few-holds-barred, rule-by-judge landscape college sports resides in, commissioners face more roadblocks to their authority, but it's notable the Big Ten does not feature infighting comparable to LSU vs. SEC, or Denny vs. Sankey.

In the land of the blind, the one-eyed man becomes king.

During COVID times, Sankey asserted himself as the man with the plan as compared to out-of-their-depth rivals like the Big Ten's Kevin Warren or the Pac-12's George Kliavkoff.

In Petitti, Warren's Big Ten successor, Sankey found himself up against a worthy foil, a two-eyed man with an insatiable appetite for a super-sized playoff.

SEC membership tasked Sankey with getting a 16-team playoff plan across the finish line. He trumpeted support for a 16-team model as recently as 12 months ago.

"The move to 16 should be a priority," Sankey said last November.

Coaches and ADs became frustrated that Sankey couldn't deliver on an expanded playoff, after he'd persuaded membership to toughen their schedules with a ninth conference game. When Sankey failed to achieve his objective of a 16-team playoff, SEC support peeled off in favor of 24 teams.

The SEC championship, which Sankey said he was "pretty committed" to as recently as May, became a casualty of a 24-team playoff.

There's a joke in there somewhere about the SEC trading its lucrative championship game so that Southern Cal could finally make the playoff.

Legislation efforts magnetize too much of Sankey's attention. He fell into the trap of thinking the federal government could solve college sports' issues and took his eye off matters closer to home.

Like, why is the SEC the only Power Four conference that can't manage to provide TV viewers with audio of its replay reviews?

Big Ten football teams winning three consecutive national championships affected Sankey's reputation, too, just as the SEC's longtime dominance previously boosted it.

Commissioners don't call plays or throw passes, but perception is reality, and championships make for effective imagery. When Petitti spoke at Big Ten media days last summer alongside three national championship trophies, it painted a powerful portrait.

I asked Sankey before this season about the Big Ten's ascent into college football's pole position and what he could do to reverse that trend. Sankey refuted the notion entirely and insisted metrics he'd reviewed privately maintained that the SEC remained the best conference "by far." If an SEC team triumphs this season, he'll feel vindicated.

At Sankey's peak, he saved the 2020 season after the Big Ten and Pac-12 panicked. Around that time, he also struck a lucrative deal to make ABC and ESPN to be the SEC's exclusive media rights partners. Consider that a tally in Sankey's wins column. The SEC dominates TV ratings and the conversation on the ABC/ESPN dials.

Sankey built on the momentum of his triumphant 2020 by snapping up Texas and Oklahoma for the SEC's ranks in 2021. A power move, from a man who'd grown into the role of commissioner as Mike Slive's heir and authored a legacy of his own.

His more recent influence is seen in the CFP rankings. Sankey and the SEC persuaded the selection committee to more seriously weight strength of schedule. That's reflected in the SEC having nine teams in the top 25, including four four-loss teams.

Given his past accomplishments, the simplest answer to Sankey's backslide might be that he simply remained in office too long, a mistake he might've observed from all the hours he spent these last years rubbing elbows with politicians.

When Sankey's not pressing the flesh of politicos, he's on "Finebaum" griping about TV broadcasters.

It's like he's torn between being Lobbyist Sankey or Average Greg.

Lost in the middle is the man who used to be an effective commissioner and college football's most powerful person.

Blake Toppmeyer is the USA TODAY Network's senior national college football columnist. Listen to his podcast, " College Football Unfiltered ." Email him at BToppmeyer@gannett.com and follow him on X @btoppmeyer .

articles.title: ACC football tiebreakers: Can Miami, Wake Forest make ACC a two-bid CFP league?
articles.summary: With two weeks left in the regular season, two teams are on track to reach the ACC title game. But chaos isn't far away. A look at the tiebreakers.
articles.body:
Whether the ACC can place two teams in the College Football Playoff depends on clean finishes by Miami and Wake Forest.

To have a shot, the Hurricanes and Demon Deacons must be 11-1 when they meet in the conference championship game. Each would have a very strong loss: Miami to Notre Dame (31-24) and Wake to the Hurricanes (33-20).

Should both be 11-1, a Wake win in the ACC title game would avenge that earlier loss and give the Demon Deacons a chance at a top-four finish and bye into the playoff quarterfinals. Miami would have a very strong argument for the playoff by citing two losses to fellow playoff teams and the earlier win against Wake.

If that scenario flips, it's not certain the Demon Deacons would get in as an at-large pick. That would depend on some messiness elsewhere, such as whether Utah is the lone Big 12 representative or if the Utes lose the conference championship game and are joined in the 12-team field by Texas Tech or Brigham Young.

These are stakes as the ACC heads to the finish line. These tiebreakers will determine which two teams meet to decide the conference title early next month:

Contenders: Miami (7-0), Wake Forest (6-1), Louisville (6-2).

Miami can book its spot in the ACC championship with a win this weekend against Virginia Tech. The Hurricanes can also advance with a win against Boston College next Saturday.

Wake is also very close to locking things down. The Demon Deacons have two clear paths to a rematch with Miami:

One, by winning out against Georgia Tech and Duke. That would leave Wake at least a game ahead of Louisville even if the Cardinals beat Pittsburgh this week.

Or two, by splitting the next two. Even if Louisville wins against the Panthers, Wake would finish in second place because of a head-to-head win (30-27) against the Cardinals.

Louisville is in a tight spot. Because of that loss to Wake, the Cardinals would need to beat Pittsburgh while the Demon Deacons lose out.

The way things get chaotic is if the Demon Deacons do end up losing twice. This isn't easy to picture: Wake has won six in a row by a combined score of 313-38.

Picture this scenario. Wake loses twice and finishes 6-3. Louisville loses to Pittsburgh to finish 6-3. SMU and Duke also win out for a four-way tie for second place.

If so, the ACC would break the tie by using the SportsSource Analytics rankings. While there's no way to know exactly how those rankings would look in two weeks, the Blue Devils' win against Wake could be deciding factor in sending them back to the conference title game.

articles.title: El Barça 'mima' a Hamza
articles.standfirst: El club asegura abiertamente que será uno de los mejores delanteros del mundo
articles.summary: El club asegura abiertamente que será uno de los mejores delanteros del mundo
articles.body: Hamza se dio a conocer en el pasado Mundial. Pocos sabían del joven delantero que el Barcelona había incorporado en calidad de cedido el invierno pasado y que militaba en el Juvenil. Sin embargo, la llamada de Egipto para la gran cita de selecciones lo puso en el escaparate y el club no tardó en hacer efectiva su opción de compra, de 1,5 millones de euros. De hecho, la entidad tiene una fe ciega en el delantero y, desde la Dirección Deportiva, están convencidos de que será uno de los mejores '9' del mundo. Y no pierden la oportunidad de expresarlo públicamente. Tras un verano en el que el debate sobre el '9' estuvo encima de la mesa, Hansi Flick acertó al reubicar a Raphinha como delantero centro. Ahora no hay dudas de que la posición está bien cubierta y, desde el club, tienen claro que el futuro está en manos del egipcio. Bojan sigue muy de cerca su evolución, como hace con todos los jóvenes, y está convencido del potencial del internacional. "Es que tenemos a los mejores delanteros del mundo. Es más, tenemos uno que es joven y que será uno de los mejores. Hamza Abdelkarim ha demostrado en pretemporada su olfato goleador, algo difícil de encontrar y que tenemos nosotros", aseguró con orgullo Bojan durante una entrevista concedida a Catalunya Ràdio el miércoles. El club dejó así muy clara la confianza que tiene en el internacional, pese a los pocos minutos de los que está disfrutando a las órdenes de Hansi Flick. Por el momento, aunque es un habitual en las convocatorias, solo ha disputado 12 minutos repartidos en dos encuentros. Incluso, a mediados de octubre reforzó al Barça Atlètic frente al Utebo, en un compromiso en el que fue titular y en el que, además, marcó un gol. Tal y como adelantó MARCA hace un par de días, pese al escaso protagonismo del jugador, ni el club ni Hamza se plantean una salida en este mercado de enero. Las palabras de Bojan de ayer refuerzan aún más esta idea. La confianza en el futbolista es total. El Barça está convencido de que será uno de los mejores delanteros del mundo.

articles.title: La gran decisión
articles.standfirst: Vini, que llega de anotar cinco goles con Brasil, reclama su hueco ante Mourinho y 'amenaza' a Diomande y Güler
articles.summary: Vini, que llega de anotar cinco goles con Brasil, reclama su hueco y 'amenaza' a Diomande y Güler
articles.body: El Real Madrid retoma la competición ante el Celta, el sábado en el Bernabéu. La hinchada tiene ganas de ver a los suyos, que llegan de firmar, casi todo a domicilio, un periplo perfecto entre los dos primeros parones internacionales del curso. La ventana FIFA, muchas veces incómoda para los clubes, puede ser balsámica para los jugadores. El cambio de entorno puede ser beneficioso. Y no hay mejor ejemplo de este dualidad que Vinicius Junior. El brasileño, castigado en España con una sanción de cuatro partidos que acabó en Mestalla, ha aprovechado el parón para cargar pilas. En dos amistosos que ni siquiera ha jugado completos (90 y 60 minutos, respectivamente) ha anotado cinco goles, algunos de ellos espectacular, para reivindicarse después de un arranque de curso turbulento. El propio delantero reconoció en conferencia de prensa previa al duelo ante Singapur que su verano no fue el mejor de los posibles desde el punto de vista de la preparación y el cuidado físico. Además de en los espacios deportivos, su nombre apareció en medios más vinculados al mundo del corazón. Incluso un pequeño retoque estético disparó las más absurdas teorías de la conspiración sobre el extremo. A todo ello se suma, además, la renovación con el Real Madrid, sellada también en verano, que refrenda su estatus como uno de los jugadores franquicia del club. Hubo ofertas, algunas de mucho calado, pero la prioridad del jugador siempre fue seguir en el Bernabéu. Y la del club siempre fue renovarle. Pero ese acuerdo, como admitió el propio Vini, puso más presión sobre sus hombros. La temprana eliminación de Brasil en el Mundial (cayó en octavos de final ante Noruega) acabó de formar la tormenta perfecta sobre la psique del jugador, acostumbrada a lidiar con toneladas de presión, casi siempre de forma exitosa. Los cinco goles de Vini ante Japón (dos) y y Singapur (tres) son su mejor aval para volver a un once liguero del Madrid, algo que está por verse este próximo sábado. Durante su larga ausencia, Yan Diomande se ha hecho fuerte en su posición, el extremo izquierdo. Los resultados, y el juego, avalan la candidatura del marfileño, que cuenta a su favor con su capacidad para jugar también por la derecha. Pero ahí aparece otro problema, y no menor. Ahí está brillando Arda Güler, para muchos la clave del crecimiento del Madrid en los últimos partidos. Nadie ve al turco fuera del once ante el Celta, por mucho que haya sumado muchos minutos con Turquía en el parón, algo que, por otra parte, han hecho la gran mayoría de internacionales madridistas. Así, con Mbappé y Bellingham como intocables, tres jugadores se reparten dos puestos, aunque las molestias de Tchouaméni pueden habilitar un espacio extra en el doble pivote, en el que Arda podría acompañar a Bernardo Silva, otro de los protagonistas del cremiento del equipo, sobre todo con balón. Sería, en cualquier caso, una solución de emergencia, ya que ni Güler ni Bernardo son prodigios físicos ni expertos en recuperaciones, pero al menos daría a José Mourinho margen de maniobra. Una oportunidad de volver a ver juntos a Vini y Diomande, y que sea el balón el que decida. Porque lo que es evidente es que, con todos sanos, sobra talento pero faltan huecos cuando todos los futbolistas, como parece ahora, están listos y afilados.

articles.title: FIFA confirms Diallo, Tashima as Infantino’s challengers at 2027 election
articles.summary: French football chief Philippe Diallo and Japan’s Kozo Tashima will be the only candidates to run for FIFA presidency.
articles.body:
FIFA president Gianni ⁠⁠Infantino’s re-election bid ⁠⁠will be challenged by the French and Japanese federations’ presidents, Philippe Diallo and Kozo Tashima , football’s global governing body has confirmed.

Former Swiss defender Ramon Vega, who announced his intention to run last month, was not among the candidates FIFA mentioned on Thursday.

The ⁠⁠election, set to be held in March 2027, will be the first time Infantino faces a challenger after being re-elected without opposition in 2023.

French Football Federation (FFF) president Diallo announced his candidacy on Monday, with the support of ‌‌UEFA member associations represented on the executive committee and the FIFA Council.

Tashima, the Japanese Federation’s Association president, declared his bid earlier this month and formally submitted his nomination on Wednesday.

“The candidatures have been forwarded to the electoral committee for examination and for passing a decision on the admission of the candidates,” FIFA said in a ⁠⁠statement.

“Member associations will be notified of the names ⁠⁠of the proposed and admitted candidates no later than 18 February 2027.”

Infantino has faced repeated calls for his resignation since his FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal , a bid to sell ⁠⁠stakes in the World Cup and other major competitions, failed.

But the 56-year-old Swiss native, who has ⁠⁠been the FIFA president since 2016, maintains that ⁠⁠he has enough support from member associations around the world to get him re-elected.

Diallo, who took over as FFF president in 2023, played a leading role as France and ‌‌other European associations withdrew their support from Infantino this year over the FFE controversy.

“Against the backdrop of serious concerns over the direction of ‌‌FIFA, ‌‌the national associations called for renewed unity and trust within the global football community,” UEFA said on Monday.

articles.title: Everton: How Premier League's 'sleeping giant' are exceeding expectations ahead of Brentford test
articles.summary: After a difficult summer, Everton are proving greater than the sum of their parts with another European push and some battling performances; watch Brentford vs Everton live on Sky Sports Premier League and Main Event from 6.30pm on Monday Night Football; kick-off 8pm
articles.body:
Moyes has said for some time that the Toffees need more bodies, but for all of his public declarations, Everton have been left with just 18 senior players and one recognised striker until January.

Coming so soon after a late-season collapse saw them miss out on European football, it is understandable why Moyes was left frustrated and some tipped them for relegation form.

"My expectations changed during the window," the Scotsman said recently. "I don't think Everton are ever going to spend hundreds and hundreds of millions to improve so all I can do is take a small progression, get a bit better every year and that felt it was going to be much harder, but the players are doing a brilliant job with their league position."

Any expectations have been exceeded. Everton are mounting another European push, currently sixth in the Premier League - just two points from the top four. They are also into quarter-finals of the Carabao Cup, facing Fleetwood in the final eight next month.

"It's a massive club, a sleeping giant of the English game," Everton midfielder Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall told Sky Sports . "I really want to do something with this club or win some silverware and give the fans something to scream about."

While it remains early in the season, the belief and confidence is clear. The Toffees are proving greater than the sum of their parts as their upward trajectory under Moyes continues.

It hasn't all been easy points for Everton - they have had to work hard for them. In two draws against Bournemouth and Manchester United , they did not score before the 83rd minute. They needed an 80th minute goal from Charly Alcaraz to beat Wolves in the third round of the Carabao Cup.

The Toffees also went behind to Coventry in their last Premier League match before the international break, going on to win 3-1. Admittedly, that game came with its own dose of luck for Everton, but fans might argue that it is about time they were on the right end of things.

After that game on Friday Night Football, Dewsbury-Hall said: "Our mentality this year has gone from strength to strength... we just never know when we're out of the game. Every time we have gone behind this season, we've reacted in a positive manner."

And just as importantly, they have seen out games when needed. There have been wins and clean sheets against Crystal Palace , Ipswich and Newcastle . They also swept the Magpies aside in the Carabao Cup fourth round with a convincing 3-1 win.

They have only lost twice - at home to Chelsea and away to Premier League champions, Arsenal . Neither result was disastrous.

In-form players boosting attacking output

After beating Newcastle in the Premier League, Moyes said: "We're creating chances. That's the big thing for me. We want to be a side that creates more chances. If we could be more offensive, that's the way I'd like it to be."

And Moyes is getting his wish. Everton are largely matching or exceeding their numbers from last season. While the number of goals scored per games is roughly the same, they are registering more shots and have a higher xG.

A big part of that is down to the form of their only recognised striker Thierno Barry . "He's come back off the summer like a different player," team-mate Dewsbury-Hall said.

He is playing far more centrally than last year - where he spent more time on the right wing - and is close to surpassing most of his attacking numbers from the entirety of last season with only ten games played. He has also scored in three successive games for Everton for the first time. Suddenly, the Frenchman is discovering a taste for goals that even the most optimistic Evertonian would have struggled to predict.

However, he has missed more big chances than any other Premier League player this season (16) - twice as many as the player in second, Bournemouth's Rayan (8). It suggests he has actually been anything but clinical, and if he had a better finishing touch, he could be an early frontrunner for the Golden Boot. His continued improvement in that part of his game is going to be vital for Everton.

Another in-form playing having a huge influence is Dewsbury-Hall himself.

Sky Sports pundit Jamie Redknapp was full of praise for the midfielder after his display against Coventry, especially in the No 10 role, running forward with and without the ball to push Everton up the pitch.

"I'm really enjoying it," the former Chelsea and Leicester man said of his role in that game. "I've got a really good hybrid role in this team where the gaffer has given me license to pop up all over the pitch.

"I feel like I'm getting a good relationship with Thierno now and I'm buzzing he keeps getting the goals because he deserves it so much... as long as he keeps performing, I'll keep trying to help him as much as I can."

Moyes is the Premier League's most experienced manager. Monday's game at Brentford will see him overtake Harry Catterick's record of the most Everton games managed, moving on to 493.

Across his career, he has stabilised clubs, won silverware, and worked with fewer resources than may be available at some other Premier League clubs - elements he has had to contend with in his second spell at Everton.

When he took over for a second time in January 2025, Everton were staring down another relegation battle, sitting 16th in the table, a point above the relegation places. They eventually finished in 13th, 23 points clear of the drop.

And last season, the Toffees were rarely spoken about as relegation contenders. While it was a disappointing finish, Moyes had once again stabilised a club who are one of six ever-presents in the Premier League.

But the Everton boss is a realist and while they are exceeding expectations at the moment, Moyes is keen to keep feet on the ground. "I don't mind building expectations but somewhere along the lines someone will turn around and say, 'have you actually had a look at the size of their squad and the players they've got?'," he said.

"Maybe when you get to that point, you start saying, 'wait a minute, calm yourself down a little bit'. I'm not using it as an excuse, I'm just telling you around the corner there could be things that don't go for us."

Of course, a lot of that will stem from last season's disappointment at missing out on Europe and an underlying concern that Everton could drop off once again.

They failed to win any of their last seven Premier League games in the 2025/26 campaign, which ultimately saw them slip out of European contention, finishing 13th.

That will still be fresh in the mind and Moyes will want to increase his squad size in January to ensure history does not repeat itself. Sky Sports News reported this week that a striker to support Barry and right-back are key for the upcoming window.

We also have to keep in mind that there have only been 10 Premier League games played - not even a third of the season - and anything can happen between now and May.

But so far, Everton are heading in the right direction and will have learnt from previous failures. Good players and good managers - of which they have both - always do.

"There's a feel-good factor about Everton right now. David Moyes has done a great job," Redknapp said a few weeks ago. The Toffees will be hoping that lasts for the next seven months and beyond.

articles.title: Argentina mourns teen footballer Nunez who died after on-pitch collision
articles.summary: Abel Nunez, 16, died after suffering a severe blow to the head during a youth football match for his club, Ezeiza.
articles.body:
Football fans and players in Argentina are mourning the death of teenage footballer Abel Nunez, who died after suffering a head injury during a youth match last week.

Nunez suffered a severe blow to the head during a fifth division youth match between his club FC Ezeiza and Muniz on Friday and died two days later, according to reports in Argentinian media.

Shortly after the on-field incident, the 16-year-old’s club posted a statement saying he suffered a “severe head injury that required surgery” and called on supporters to participate in a prayer chain.

Following his death, Argentine social media was flooded with an outpouring of shock and messages of condolence for Nunez’s family and friends, said Argentinian news outlet TN Deportivo.

“With profound sorrow and immense sadness, we say goodbye to a young man who had his whole life ahead of him and who today leaves us with a void impossible to describe,” his club said.

“After suffering a hard blow during a match, proudly wearing our Ezeiza shirt, we deeply regret his departure.

“Today football is in the background. We are overwhelmed by the pain of saying goodbye to a colleague, a young man full of dreams and hopes, who was part of our family.

“May you rest in peace. You will always be part of our family.”

Born in 2008, Nunez was a native of Ezeiza, a city within the Greater Buenos Aires region. He played both football and futsal regularly, according to the information he shared on his Facebook profile.

Nunez’s futsal team, Nueva Estrella, also joined in the mourning and announced a suspension of activities.

“You will always be with us. Your memory will live forever in our hearts,” the club wrote on social media.

Roman Corral, the father of the teenager’s best friend, gave a heartbreaking account of how the young man’s teammates and loved ones are coping with their grief.

“The boys are devastated; it’s something unnatural for them. At that age, you think you’re a superhero, and to lose your life like that, the way Abel lost his… I’ve known him since he was 12, when he started school with my son in first grade. His dream was to be a football player, just like my son,” Corral told Radio La Red in Argentina.

Corral used the radio programme to send a direct message to the Argentine football authorities: “If anyone from the AFA is listening, please observe a minute of silence. He wanted to live as a footballer and he should be given a send-off as a footballer because he died on the pitch, doing what all Argentinians love, which is playing football.”

articles.title: Championship: The tightest and highest-scoring promotion race ever?
articles.summary: With five teams separated by just one point at the top of the Championship, could this be the best season yet?
articles.body:
Many supporters often like to label the Championship "the best league in the world".

It might be a throwaway comment, but it is one founded on the premise that the level of unpredictability and drama is unmatched.

And there is a case to be made that the Championship is living up to its unofficial tag more than ever this season.

We have seen astonishing comebacks, goals galore, unexpected results - and one third of the way through the 2026-27 campaign, you could throw a blanket over the top half of the table.

With just one point between the top five sides and eight points separating leaders Birmingham City down to Blackburn Rovers in 13th after 15 games, is this shaping up to be one of, if not the best promotion and play-off contests ever in the second tier?

"This is going to be fun," said 72+ EFL podcast host Aaron Paul.

Jobi McAnuff, who won the Championship with Reading in 2011-12, agrees.

"It's been a brilliant start of the season. I think there's such a lovely open nature to the league so far," McAnuff said.

"You certainly wouldn't have expected West Brom right up there. Stoke... Mark Robins again doing brilliantly, and Birmingham sitting top of the table."

Former Bromley manager Andy Woodman described it as "anyone's league".

"This Championship is relentless," Woodman said. "I'm looking at all the clubs in there and Scott Parker's record of getting out of the league. He's now at West Ham sitting just behind them ready to come up.

"It is going to be an unbelievable finish to the season and if we were to call it, I don't think we could."

The final game before the two-week international break epitomised just how close the race is, and gives us plenty of reason for excitement when the Championship returns this weekend.

It is usually a rare and precious moment when football fans are able to serenade their heroes with 'We are top of the league' on the terraces.

But no less than four sets of supporters were able to do so in the space of a few hours on the afternoon of Saturday, 7 November.

The name at the top of the table changed eight times between 12:54 GMT and 16:51 GMT that day, with Birmingham eventually securing pole position.

That was only after Wolves , Stoke and Middlesbrough had led the way, however briefly, earlier in the day.

The table after 15 games is as tight as it has been since Opta started compiling statistics in 2004, although there is one other season in which just one point separated the top five sides beyond this point in a campaign, and boy, was it a doozy.

In early March 2015 Roy Hodgson was still England manager and Prime Minister David Cameron led a Conservative/Lib Dem coalition in Westminster.

Meanwhile, 36 games into the Championship season, this is what the title race looked like...

Bournemouth went on to pick up 24 points from their final 10 games to win the title and promotion to the top flight for the first time with 90 points, one ahead of Watford, who also went up.

Norwich and Middlesbrough had to settle for the play-offs, finishing third and fourth on 86 and 85 points respectively, while Brentford and Ipswich sneaked into the play-offs on goal difference, with Wolves missing out after also finishing on 78 points.

Derby ended up in eighth after taking only 17 points from their final 10 games to miss the play-offs by a point.

The table only tells half the story, however.

The Hornets would have been champions had they not conceded a late equaliser against Sheffield Wednesday on the final afternoon while the Rams had just needed to avoid defeat to secure a top-six finish, only to go down 3-0 at home to lowly Reading.

We can only hope 1 May 2027 provides us with half as much drama on the final day of the regular season.

With eight play-off places now up for grabs, the odds are it might even exceed it.

And we can all take heart from the fact the table now is slightly tighter than the one in 2014-15 was after 15 games, while it's worth noting that only one of those top five fell away in the run-in.

Does that suggest our three promoted sides will come from the current top five?

If you want lots of goals and a tense battle at the top, then look no further than the Championship.

No other league in Europe is as tightly contested right now.

The Dutch Eredivisie comes closest with three points separating the top five, compared to just one point in the Championship.

However, the season is only nine games old in the Netherlands, as opposed to 15 in the English second tier.

Only two points separate the top four in the Belgian Pro League after 11 matches but there is a nine-point gap from first to fifth.

And it is not just the promotion race delivering so far this season - the entire division is coming up with the goods in terms of entertainment.

The last time goals were banged in at a higher rate in the second tier, England were about to win the World Cup for the first and only time to date.

This season's ratio of 2.96 goals per game is the highest in the 60 years since there were 3.08 per game across the 1965-66 campaign.

With 532 goals already netted in the Championship, we are on course for a total of 1,633 should the trend continue.

That would be the highest number of goals achieved at this level since 1957-58 when there were 1,637.

The highest number of goals ever in the second tier was in 1926-27, when there were 22 teams in the division and fewer games played overall (462) compared to today (552).

Predicting the completely unpredictable might be a futile task, particularly this season.

But Opta's Supercomputer has tried to do just that by crunching the numbers to estimate the likely outcome of every remaining match using its power rankings tool and betting odds.

Opta's model considers the strength of opponents and simulates the remaining fixtures thousands of times.

The results? Middlesbrough will win the title with Wolves gaining the second automatic promotion spot.

Birmingham, Stoke, West Brom and Southampton are predicted to finish in the play-offs, as are Swansea , though they will have to do so without boss Vitor Matos who has left for French Ligue 1 club Strasbourg , while Opta expect West Ham to replace QPR in the top eight.

Woodman believes Parker's experience will help the Hammers recover from their recent blip, which prompted the club to sack boss Nuno Espirito Santo and replace him with their former midfielder.

"He knows this league inside out," said Woodman. "I'd be hard pressed to say who's better equipped for getting teams out of this league than Scotty Parker.

"He's a phenomenal manager and I think he'll do really well at West Ham."

McAnuff believes Middlesbrough are the ones to beat.

"I love what Kim Hellberg's done," he said. "They've missed Will Lankshear the past couple of games, but I still have them as my favourites. I think anyone who's above them this year will be getting automatically promoted."

Four of the teams currently in the race will meet in the first game after the international break when Stoke host Birmingham and West Brom visit Swansea.

"One of those, maybe two, will really look at it and go: 'Why can't we be the Coventry this season?'" added McAnuff.

"There's no reason why Birmingham - with such an open start to the league, particularly going down to eight teams this year - can't at least get into the play-offs.

"They will have designs on staying higher, I'm sure of that, but I do think some of the bigger teams are going to come good later on in the season."

articles.title: Carles Puyol 'ficha' por el Inter Escaldes
articles.standfirst: Será el nuevo director de relaciones y futbol internacional
articles.summary: Será el nuevo director de relaciones y futbol internacional
articles.body: El exfutbolista del Barcelona y de la selección española Carles Puyol se ha convertido en el nuevo director de relaciones y futbol internacional del Inter Club Escaldes, club de la primera división andorrana. El exjugador, de 48 años, lleva desde principios de 2022 residiendo en el Principado y, aunque estuvo a punto de aceptar alguna propuesta de Gerard Piqué, su excompañero en el club azulgrana, para entrar en la dirección deportiva del FC Andorra, club del que este último es máximo accionista y responsable del cuerpo técnico, no la aceptó. El objetivo de su incorporación al club de Escaldes-Engordany, actual campeón de liga, es ayudar a la entidad a seguir creciendo después de haberse convertido en el primer club andorrano en acceder a una fase liga de una competición europea. "Quiero felicitar al club por todo lo que ha conseguido hasta ahora. Ganar siempre es difícil, pero mantenerse en el máximo nivel aún lo es más. El reto será continuar trabajando con la misma ambición y motivación para seguir creciendo y consiguiendo nuevos objetivos", aseguró en un comunicado el nuevo director de relaciones y fútbol internacional del Inter Club Escaldes, equipo que disputa la Liga Conferencia y es rival del Getafe. Puyol fue internacional absoluto con la selección española entre 2000 y 2013, sumando un total de 100 partidos. Con ella se proclamó campeón de Europa en 2008 y campeón del mundo en 2010. Con el Barça, dónde llegó a ser capitán, ganó 21 títulos entre su debut en 1999 y su retirada en 2014, incluyendo seis Ligas, tres Ligas de Campeones y el histórico sextete de 2009. En el Inter Club Escaldes coincidirá nuevamente con el entrenador Felip Ortiz, con quien jugó en las categorías inferiores del Barça y con quien mantiene una gran amistad.

articles.title: Andoni Iraola's Liverpool start assessed: Creating chaos, going direct and fixing leaky defence
articles.summary: Liverpool host arch-rivals Man Utd with new boss Andoni Iraola having been in charge for 10 top-flight games now; the Reds sit fourth having lost twice in the league; watch Liverpool vs Man Utd on Super Sunday on Sky Sports Premier League from 4pm; kick-off 4.30pm
articles.body:
Iraola has been in charge at Anfield for less than six months after replacing Arne Slot in June following Liverpool's dismal Premier League title defence last season under the Dutchman.

The then champions could only manage an underwhelming fifth-place finish, 24 points worse off than when winning the league in 2024-25, with Slot paying with his job as a result.

Iraola was identified as the man to not only get Liverpool back to winning ways, but to also do it in a 'heavy-metal' front-footed fashion that would get fans off their seats again after what he had achieved in three hugely successful campaigns at Bournemouth.

So, 10 league games in and with Liverpool sitting in fourth place, what exactly has Iraola changed and how much progress has he made at Anfield?

There has been a noticeable increase in intensity to Liverpool's game under Iraola this season, in stark contrast to the laboured displays that dogged much of the previous campaign under his predecessor.

In fact, at times Liverpool have started to resemble Jurgen Klopp's pressing monsters again, albeit with subtle differences, as Virgil van Dijk recently pointed out.

"It's a different era, different times," said the captain prior to the international break. "Under Jurgen, we pressed a lot with shuffling across, we tried to box them in one side, but football has changed.

"So, it's different - but what isn't different is the amount of sprints and running and trying to get the ball back as soon as possible.

* PPDA is a proxy for pressing intensity, it is the number of opposition passes allowed per defensive action

"You have to try to create this chaos, second balls, battles, and that's what we still are learning."

Part of that chaos Iraola has tried to create can be seen in how Liverpool's players man-mark all over the pitch on occasions with, for example, Van Dijk following his man all the way into the opposition half.

That, though, can create its own problems, according to the Dutchman: "It's a challenge because when teams know that we want to win the ball high they try to drag you into difficult spaces and you have to read the game."

That disruption can also be seen in the unpredictability of personnel in Liverpool's wide forward areas, with the Reds boss not only keeping the opposition guessing by changing who starts in those positions - regardless of which foot they favour - but by switching them in game as well.

And one of the positive knock-on effects of trying to get back to Klopp's 'heavy-metal' brand of football is it has reawakened Anfield.

Liverpool as a team have always tried to harness the power of the home fans and feed off them, especially under the German, but that was somewhat lost as a result of Slot's more prosaic, safety-first style of play.

But, according to the skipper, it is worth starting fast at Anfield to get the home faithful fully invested: "Especially here [Anfield], at the start, you have to go all in and take that risk. If you win the ball high, you see the crowd coming up as well and it just brings that energy that will help throughout the whole 90 minutes."

'Risk-reward' of going direct vs playing through the press

Part of that unpredictability under Iraola so far this season has also seen the back line - mainly Van Dijk - not be afraid to mix things up by going long to beat the opposition press, particularly at Anfield.

The stats certainly back this up, with Liverpool having been more direct this campaign [50.8 long passes per game] than either last season [46.3] or Klopp's final one [49.6], while the players are also winning more of their aerial duels in the process.

Consequently, that has meant more of Van Dijk's characteristic long-range crossfield passes out of defence looking for his pacy forwards to start attacks, although as the captain explains, it is now all about finding "the right balance' between the two approaches.

"Are you going to go direct and play the second ball or you're going to try go through them? That's the risk-reward you have to take," says Van Dijk.

"You have to be able to adapt and that's part of our jobs as well. The manager can obviously put the plan out but we as players have the responsibility in order to execute and win the game as well, with the help, of course, of the manager and the staff, but we on the pitch are the ones that have the most influence.

"We have to be a little bit more direct and that helps again winning the ball high.

"You have to find the right balance because I feel that we can still play through the press, but we can also go direct and at home sometimes you have to."

Araujo's arrival helps shore up leaky defence

One area where Liverpool have significantly improved from last season is defending set plays, a major Achilles' heel in Slot's final campaign.

Under the Dutchman, the Reds shipped a whopping 23 Premier League goals from set pieces - second only to the 26 let in by Iraola's Bournemouth - a weakness that in many ways came to symbolise their slipshod title defence.

Whereas so far this season, albeit across a much smaller sample size, Iraola's side have conceded twice from set plays, with the Basque crediting the training-ground work done by his assistants Tommy Elphick and Shaun Cooper.

"I think we have, touch wood, dealt very well with defending set pieces so far this season," he said.

"It definitely helps having a centre-back [Ronalds Araujo] at right-back when we talk about defending set pieces. It helps a bit with the height and the physicality of the team."

In fact, overall since Araujo was brought into the defence at Ipswich Town in September, Liverpool have only let in three league goals with 11 men on the pitch, in stark contrast to the 53 they conceded under Slot last time out, their most ever in a 38-game Premier League campaign.

Last season the then champions seemed incapable of recovering from any sort of setback, as evidenced by them picking up just the five points from losing positions all season long in what was a clear sign of their waning powers of recovery and team spirit.

But already this campaign Liverpool have managed to win the same amount of points in a come-from-behind victory at Brentford, as well as draws with Newcastle United and Nottingham Forest, in a demonstration of their will to win under Iraola.

All of which will remind Liverpool fans of Klopp's 'Mentality Monsters', who were never beaten, however grave the situation, although Iraola's side still have some way to go to match the 28 points the Reds won from losing situations in the German's final season at the helm in 2023-24.

Can Iraola make Anfield a fortress again starting against United?

Bizarrely, in contrast to their unrivalled form on the road this season, Liverpool have won just once at Anfield in the Premier League, the 2-0 victory over Brighton in October, with Iraola only too aware of utilising the power of the Reds' faithful.

"At Anfield, everyone feels when the team goes for it and when everyone is giving everything and trying their best our supporters will be there to help the team," he said.

"Even when we have started losing some of the last games, they have been there and helped us massively.

"At home we have a big advantage against teams and this atmosphere we can create, this is special."

A red-hot atmosphere can be guaranteed to greet United on Sunday, especially with the visitors arriving at Anfield in the relegation zone - so what better opponents to record just a second home win in the league since April than their arch rivals from down the East Lancs Road?

Watch Liverpool vs Man Utd on Sky Sports Premier League from 4pm; kick-off 4.30pm

articles.title: Man Utd latest financial results revealed as revenue and wages increase
articles.summary: Manchester United's latest financial results for the first fiscal quarter of 2027 covered three months up to September 30; it included the summer transfer window and their return to the Champions League, but not the sacking of Michael Carrick and arrival of Mauricio Pochettino
articles.body:
The first quarter fiscal 2027 report covered three months up to September 30. It included the summer transfer window but not the sacking of Michael Carrick and subsequent hiring of Mauricio Pochettino.

It does include the club's return to the Champions League. However, only one of these matches were at home - a 4-0 win against Sabah. They played four further games at Old Trafford, and three away.

Manchester United's total revenues rose 4.1 per cent to £146.1m compared to the same period last year, while wages are up 8.6 per cent to £79.9m.

The club's loss after tax increased by 174.2 per cent to £18.1m, with interest paid down 32 per cent to £14.5m.

Non-current borrowings - the debts associated when the Glazer family bought the club 21 years ago - are up 19.2 per cent from $650m (£481.2m) to $775m (£577.4m), primarily as a result of refinancing. Current borrowings are down from £268m to £207.1m.

In terms of personnel, player sale profits down went down 54 per cent to £20.7m. The net expenditure on intangible assets - namely players - increased by £43.3m to £143.1m.

There was 17.7 per cent in broadcasting revenue - up from £29.9m to £35.2m - which likely coincides with Manchester United's return to the Champions League.

Matchday revenue is also up 2.3 per cent from £26.2m to £26.8m, although sponsorship revenue went down three per cent from £47m to £45.6m after the men's team had a smaller pre-season tour. Retail and merchandising also went up 3.5 per cent from £37.2m to £38.5m.

Manchester United chief executive Omar Berrada said of the results: "Our revenue remains strong and on track, while we continue to grow sustainably.

"We are pleased to welcome Mauricio Pochettino and his staff to the club and our priority is to support them as we look continuously to improve our performances on the pitch.

"We are pleased with the progress Eva Olid has made with our women's team and how well the team has adapted to her approach."
